status_note: `functions_string.yaml` (substrait-extensions 0.106.0): `replace` is "Replace all occurrences of the substring with the replacement string" and says nothing of an empty substring. Not searched upstream.
summary: `replace(input, substring, replacement)` does not say what an empty `substring` matches. DuckDB returns the input unchanged (a NULL for a NULL replacement), and Polars and Rust's `str::replace` insert the replacement before every character and at the end.
repro: `replace('ab', '', 'x')`: DuckDB 2.0.0 gives `'ab'` (fact duckdb-replace-empty-pattern); Polars gives `'xaxbx'` (fact polars-string-natives).
handling: The SQL lift and the Ibis producer refuse a constant empty pattern under the reference; `semantics="duckdb"` lifts it to DuckDB's value. The DuckDB writer refuses the plan when it is handed in as Substrait (#1508).
Could be expressed as: one sentence in the description (an empty substring matches nowhere, or at every character boundary), or an option.
found_by: the text semantics of the reference (#1508)

checked.note: functions_string.yaml: replace's description and its two impls (string and varchar<L>) say nothing of an empty substring; the options are case_sensitivity only
